doc.title: Albert Warner and Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08

title: Half-brother Ulysses Jackson and Honore Dutrey
summary: Warner names his half-brother Ulysses Jackson, who played in the Excelsior band and later in Chicago with Dutrey.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: He used in California too, man. Yeah, in California. I'll get out there again sometime. See all the fellas.
I guess I'll be up there pretty soon. Not to stay.
You were just going out for a visit.
Yeah, I got my son up there. The saxophone player? Uh-huh.
Oh, what was your half-brother's name? I didn't get that.
Ulyss Jackson. I've heard of him. Oh, he's dead. He died in Chicago.

Well, he used to play with the Excelsior Band. That was years ago, you see. Then he left. He didn't stay up very long after that. Then he left and he went to Chicago. He played with Honoré Dutré. You remember when Honoré was playing with Dick Selsior? The Trumont player? Yeah. Sure. You remember that big fella? Big papers that look like a type? Oh, yeah. Yeah. That's who I'm speaking of. Oh, yeah?
Yeah. Well, something was going to say, you are annoying.
Because Honoré Lloyd Tim, you see. Yeah, I understand. Well, after Honoré Lloyd Tim, he said, well, he says, you see the Albert Lloyd in how to play. He was a good one to it.
